paper.title: Learning in Bayesian Stackelberg Games With Unknown Follower's Types

settings.name_in_paper: Online learning in Bayesian Stackelberg games with unknown follower types, type feedback
unmapped: Leader commits to a mixed strategy x in the simplex over m leader actions; follower of private type theta ~ mu (i.i.d., unknown distribution over K types) best responds with ties broken in favour of the leader
Follower payoffs of every type and the type distribution are unknown; leader's own utility function is known
Type feedback: leader observes the follower's best-response action and the realized type each round
The learner knows an upper bound L on the bit-complexity of all payoffs
Leader's expected utility is piecewise linear and discontinuous over best-response regions
Assumes an optimal commitment lies in a best-response region P(a*) with positive volume
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t \in [T]$ ... The leader commits to a mixed strategy $x_t \in \Delta(\Al)$. A follower's type $\theta_t \in \Theta$ is sampled according to $\mu$ ... Under \emph{type feedback}, the leader observes both $a_{\theta_t}^\star(x_t)$ and $\theta_t$ ... $R_T \coloneqq T \cdot \OPT - \mathbb{E}[\sum_{t \in [T]} \ul(x_t,a^\star_\theta(x_t))]$

settings.name_in_paper: Online learning in Bayesian Stackelberg games with unknown follower types, action feedback (lower bound)
unmapped: Leader commits to a mixed strategy over leader actions; follower type drawn i.i.d. from unknown distribution, follower payoffs unknown
Action feedback: leader observes only the follower's best-response action, not the type
The learner knows the bit-complexity bound L of the follower payoffs
settings.definition_quote: Under \emph{type feedback}, the leader observes both $a_{\theta_t}^\star(x_t)$ and $\theta_t$, while under \emph{action feedback}, the leader only observes the best response $a_{\theta_t}^\star(x_t)$.

conditions: instance with constant-sized leader/follower action sets and set of types (3 leader actions, 4 follower actions, 3 types, uniform type distribution)

source.label: thm:lower_bound_actionfeedback
source.quote: Let $L \in \mathbb{N}$ be the bit-complexity of the follower's payoffs. Under action feedback, for any learning algorithm, there exists a BSG instance with constant-sized leader/follower action sets and set of follower types, and $T=\Theta(2^{2L})$ rounds, such that $R_T \ge \Omega(2^{2L})$.

results.notes: Proved via Yao's minimax principle; regret linear in T since T = Theta(2^{2L}). Regret defined via expected leader utility at commitments, recorded as pseudo_regret.

symbols.B_delta: bit-complexity of the input confidence parameter delta

conditions: there exists an optimal commitment in a best-response region P(a*) of positive volume
payoffs rational with bit-complexity at most L (known to the leader)
leader utility in [0,1]; follower breaks ties in favour of the leader

source.label: th:main_formal
source.quote: With probability at least $1-\delta$, the regret of Algorithm~\ref{alg:main_algo} is: $R_T \le \Obigt(K^2 \log(\frac{K}{\delta} ) \sqrt{T} +\beta\log^2(T))$, where: $\beta \coloneqq K^{m+2} n^{2m+2} (m^7 (L+B_\delta) \log(\frac{1}{\delta}) + (Kn +m)^{m} )$ is a time-independent function of the instance size and $\delta$.

results.notes: Informal version (th:main_informal) in the main text states O~(K^2 log(1/delta) sqrt(T) + beta log^2 T) with beta = poly(n,K,L,log(1/delta)) for constant m; not recorded separately. Paper's K is number of types, m leader actions, n follower actions (renamed). R_T itself is defined as an expectation but the statement is with probability 1-delta.

cited_results.setting_description: Bayesian Stackelberg games with stochastic follower types, even when the leader knows each type's payoffs
cited_results.where: Section 4.4, On the tightness of Theorem
